Green Street isn’t really about football. It’s about identity, loyalty, and the kind of brotherhood people will risk everything to protect.

After being expelled from Harvard, Matt is thrown into the world of West Ham’s football firm, where respect is earned through loyalty rather than reputation. Charlie Hunnam commands every scene as Pete Dunham, bringing a quiet confidence and charisma that makes him one of the film’s most unforgettable characters.

Beneath the brutal fights and nonstop tension is a story about belonging, purpose, and the lengths people will go to defend the people they call family. It’s raw, emotional, and leaves a lasting impression long after the credits roll.
